definition: A familiar biblical image for a ruler or leader who protects, guides, and provides for a people. The image also emphasizes the dependence of the flock on its keeper.
The Scriptures use love for affection, friendship, and especially the deliberate self-giving care that fulfills God's command. Its fullest pattern is seen in God's action toward the world.
The created order is presented as the work of the one living God. Creation language grounds the Bible's account of God's authority and the world's dependence on him.
The unmerited favor of God toward sinners, shown in the gift of salvation and in the kindness believers are called to extend to others.
A learner who follows a teacher. Christ's disciples are called not only to receive instruction but also to make other disciples and teach them.
A place of shelter or protection. Biblical refuge language points to God as the secure defense of those who seek him in danger.
Relief from labor and distress. The invitation to come to Christ presents rest as a gracious answer to the burdened and weary.
